thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert — smart-routing / cache mismatch detected for multiple tenants. Symptoms: increased 5xx, degraded latency, routing fallback thrash. Paging oncall @sara :rotating_light:

sara: on it, acked. pulling traces now — can someone grab the routing logs and KV cache metrics for the last 15m?

alex: looking. Getting a lot of 'fallback loop detected' entries in routing-service logs. Example:
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:21Z] ERROR routing: fallback loop detected tenant=acme, route=eu-primary -> fallback=global-v1 -> both variants incompatible
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] WARN cache: kv-get miss key=kv:model:v1:tenant:acme
[2026-03-15T12:03:22Z] INFO routing: attempted serve model=global-v1 region=us fallback_count=3
```

mike: noticed cache keys are missing region suffix. Current cache key derivation in runtime is: `kv_key = "model:" + model_id + ":tenant:" + tenant_id` — but routing selection and compatibility are region-aware. If a model variant is region-scoped, reusing a cached KV (KV cache / prefixes) across regions can return incorrect KV/activation tokens.

jess: that lines up with customer reports — calls from EU are being served by US variants after fallback, causing semantic mismatches and some auth errors. We have 12 affected customers top-of-funnel, ~0.7% of overall requests but concentrated on high-SLA tenants.

sara: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) disable auto-fallback policy globally (so no cross-region fallthrough) 2) flush KV-prefix caches for affected tenants 3) pin routing to region-specific compatible model variants for the hot path 4) create alert to detect region/kv signature mismatch. Agree?

alex: agree. Executing step 1 now — toggling routing.fallback.enabled=false via the control plane.

incident-bot: Control plane change applied by alex (runbook: disable fallback) — version 2026-03-15_12:05.

mike: doing cache flush for the EU pool. Running:
```
curl -s -X POST https://ops-api.redwood.internal/v1/cache/flush \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prefix":"kv:model:", "scope":"region:eu"}'
```
Result: started job job_id=flush-20260315-eu-01 (estimated 30s)

jess: rolling out a temporary hotfix to key derivation to include region — will push a binary with a guard flag so we can revert quickly. Patch: `kv_key = "region:"+region+":model:"+model_id+":tenant:"+tenant_id`. Building and testing in staging now.

tom: quick customer impact note — CS reported two enterprise customers seeing degraded responses and one error spike that triggered their internal SLO alert. Reached out and told them we're mitigating; escalation docs invoked.

sara: after disabling fallback and flushing EU caches, request rate errors dropped ~85% for the impacted tenants. Latency returned to normal for most requests. Still seeing intermittent wrong-model responses for requests that hit stale KV in global caches.

alex: turning on a temporary traffic-route lock for high-SLA tenants to pin to region-only routing. Command:
```
redwoodctl routes lock --tenant acme --scope region --reason "incident 2026-03-15"
```
Applied. Monitoring.

mike: deploy of region-prefixed cache key hotfix is ready. Plan: staged rollout to runtime-eu pool (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with short monitoring windows. If we see any errors, the guard flag allows immediate revert.

jess: deployment started to eu-runtime replicas (canary 10%). Observability: cache hit ratio improved for region-scoped keys, and we see no increase in 5xx during canary. Proceeding to 50%.

incident-bot: Deploy canary success. Canary metrics: 0.2% error delta, hit ratio +12% for region keys.

sara: once full rollout completes, we should re-enable fallback but only to compatible model variants (matching architecture & region compatibility). For now keep global fallback off.

mike: full rollout complete to eu-runtime at 12:28. Cache key change in prod. Running verification: verifying no cross-region kv reads via:
```
SELECT count(*) FROM cache_audit WHERE read_region != write_region AND timestamp > now()-600s;
```
Result: 0 (post-flush + hotfix).

alex: customer-facing summary for ops/CS: short outage window ~12:02–12:24 UTC, affected ~0.7% requests, escalated customers saw degraded responses, mitigations applied: disabled auto-fallback, flushed EU caches, pinned high-SLA tenants to region routing, deployed kv-key hotfix.

jess: assigning postmortem owner — jess will author. Target: initial draft in 24h, full RCA in 72h. Will include timeline, config diff, and suggested config guardrails:
- require region inclusion in any cache key that is used by routing
- validate fallback compatibility: only fallback to models with a compatible region/architecture tag
- add an automated test that simulates cross-region cache reuse
- add an alert when routing fallback count > 3 for >1m for a tenant

tom: note for product: consider a runtime lint for rollout configs that would reject a routing policy with fallback enabled + cross-region cache scope.

sara: oncall handoff — i'm wrapping up, handing to alex for overnight monitoring. alex, take it?

alex: taking handoff. I'll leave a watch on the incident dashboard and escalate if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated. Severity: P1 (mitigated). Postmortem owner: jess. Follow-up task created: TASK-1284 (runtime: enforce kv key contract).

mike: small follow-up — we discovered the original misconfig: a routing policy change earlier this week added a fallback rule for some tenants without marking model variants as region-compatible. The policy UI allowed the change because it didn't validate cache key implications. I'll open an infra PR to add validation checks.

jess: thanks all. I'll start the postmortem doc and link infra PRs/patches. If anyone has logs or traces to drop, paste them in this thread.

sara: thanks team. ending pager now. :white_check_mark:
